findings.reason: The protected source is the standard at-most-one-zero sliding window. Its left and right boundaries, zero_count invariant, validity-repair loop, and best-length update are concise, conventional, and immediately explainable in an interview, so no inert candidate is materially justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 487 and its Python binary-array contract. The implementation returns the longest contiguous segment that can be all ones after at most one zero flip, including the no-flip case. Monotonic boundaries establish the manifest's O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2065021703. It and the protected app source have identical left, zero_count, and best initialization; right/value enumeration; zero admission; while-loop repair using nums[left]; left advancement; window-length update; and return. Differences are limited to the native class/type wrapper.

The all-one workloads of lengths 32, 128, and 512 span 16x and require a full scan while maximizing repeated work for a restart-based comparator. The protected source passed all 8 correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the legal 100,000-value alternating boundary. A correct worst-case quadratic restart control with a zero-dense shortcut passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict with relative growth exponent +1.27 and a 484.39x largest runtime ratio.

The current-targeted Approach exactly follows the inclusive [left, right] window, zero_count updates, validity repair, best update, and monotonic-boundary complexity. It proves optimality per right endpoint and explains the source follow-up's constant-state last-zero adaptation without falsely attributing that different data flow to the protected implementation.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the authenticated Premium statement. It preserves the at-most-one-flip contract, both examples and every comparison in their explanations, both constraints, the infinite-stream follow-up, source section order, and the absence of visuals or tables.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with exact binary-array and result facts, and both are explicitly tagged as source examples.
The invented all-one sample is now a trial and both formerly hidden rows are visible trials. Boundaries cover array lengths 1 and 100,000 and both legal values 0 and 1.

Visible cases cover the optional no-flip path, one flippable zero, multiple competing zeros, all zeros, all ones, exclusion of an earlier zero, equal best flips, and maximum-length alternating input that repeatedly advances the left boundary.

An independent zero-position-gap oracle verified all eight authored results and all three benchmark outputs. A direct flip-enumerating brute-force oracle covered all 8,190 binary arrays through length 12 and 1,000 deterministic randomized arrays.
All eight correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged length-32, length-128, and length-512 all-one workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
